current_date: Date of last review: 6 August 2026 (applies to applications received after 6 August 2026)
current_evidence: The authority's Planning guides page (lakedistrict.gov.uk/?page_id=5337), under 'Validation guides', links 'Validation checklist' to the 'Post-6-August-2026-updated-BNG' PDF, whose text says 'Date of last review: 6 August 2026'.

issues.detail: Grokbot's link still opens, but that checklist has been superseded. The Planning guides page now links the 6 August 2026 checklist, which applies to all applications received after that date. The main change is a rewritten Biodiversity Net Gain section (13): new exemptions for householder development and for sites of 0.2 ha or less with no priority habitat impact, and self-build/custom build is no longer exempt. Ground levels (existing and proposed) were also added to Plans (section 3).
issues.evidence: Current checklist: 'Date of last review: 6 August 2026'; 'Self-build and custom-build dwellings are no longer exempt after 6 August 2026'

issues.detail: The workbook gives 2024-04-01, but the linked document's text says 'Date of last review 2 April 2024' (applies to applications received after 5 April 2024). The filename says 'August 2025', which matches neither date. The current list is dated 6 August 2026.
issues.evidence: Workbook-linked PDF: 'Date of last review: 2 April 2024'

issues.detail: Several local requirements were not captured at all: Wind Energy pre-submission consultation (2 or more wind turbines or any hub height over 15m; not for s73) (s5); Tree Constraints Plan (development other than change of use at or below ground level within 15m of trees) (s9); Non-Mains Drainage details/questionnaire, percolation tests and EA permit status (providing or altering non-mains drainage) (s12); Bat Surveys (roof, eaves or wall works to traditional/slate/stone buildings especially within 400m of woodland or water, works to tunnels/mines/kilns/bridges, floodlighting of churches/listed buildings/green space near woodland or water, felling or lopping of woodland, hedgerows or veteran trees, and wind turbines) (s15); Commercial, Business and Services impact assessment (over 1,250 sq m net outside Primary Shopping Areas) (s18); Heritage Impact Assessment for the World Heritage Site (s7, see the separate issue); ground levels on elevations/sections where levels change or basements/trenches are proposed (s3, current list only); Shadow Habitats Regulations Assessment as part of Nutrient Neutrality Option 1 (s19).
issues.evidence: Checklist sections 5, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 19 (Option 1: budget calculator, mitigation strategy, shadow HRA)

issues.detail: The row 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' is really section 7, Heritage Impact Assessment (Appendix 3). It is required for EIA development and for schemes screened at pre-application stage as affecting the Outstanding Universal Value of the Lake District World Heritage Site. The checklist does not require an Environmental Statement.
issues.evidence: Section 7: Heritage Impact Assessment required for 'environmental impact assessment development and / or any application which we have screened ... Outstanding Universal Value of the Lake District World Heritage Site'

issues.detail: Some rows are invented from stray text. 'Sunlight to gardens/amenity space' (excerpt 'required in garden areas A Limestone Pavement Area') comes from the Construction Method Statement section, where a Local Geological Site is 'not required in garden areas'; no sunlight requirement exists. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' reuses the Construction Method Statement excerpt; no such item exists. 'Self-build / custom build information' is a BNG exemption, not a requirement, and in the current list self-build is no longer exempt.
issues.evidence: Section 14 CMS: 'Local Geological Site (not required in garden areas)'

issues.detail: Most other triggers are tick-box fragments with the real trigger missing. Tree Survey: 'Tree Surveys yes If yes, a full tree survey is required... 11.' (real trigger: development in the RPA or under the canopy of trees on the tree constraints plan, or in Ancient Semi-Natural Woodland). Energy: 'yes Are Energy Statement requirements met? no 12.' (real trigger: new housing, or 100 sq m or more of new floorspace). Ecological: 'above, an Ecological Assessment is required' (real trigger: hydro scheme, within or next to a lake, within 15m of ASNW). Construction Method Statement: fragment (real trigger: demolition over 50 cu m, in/near SAC/SSSI/CWS/Ramsar/limestone pavement, in or on banks of watercourse/lake). FRA: 'If the answer is yes to any of the above' (real trigger: FZ2/3, FZ1 1 ha or more, Main River buffer, surface water risk). Heritage: 'Access and Heritage Statement is required.' (real trigger: major development, 1+ houses, 100 sq m+, LBC, listed curtilage, Conservation Area, SAM, registered park). Noise and Ventilation are the same fragment (real trigger: ventilation/extraction equipment or a new commercial kitchen). BNG excerpt is a fragment of the self-build exemption.

Householder and Listed building consent are shown as '(none)', which is wrong. Section 6 names 'Listed building consent' as a trigger for the Design, Access and Heritage Statement, and householder works in a Conservation Area or listed curtilage also trigger it. Householder schemes can also need a Tree Constraints Plan/Tree Survey, Bat Survey (roof/eaves/wall works), FRA, Non-mains drainage and Construction Method Statement. Outline/Reserved matters marked '(none)' also ignore FRA, SuDS (major) and Heritage Impact Assessment. All other requirements are placed under 'Full planning' with 'INFERRED' notes, although the checklist applies them by trigger regardless of application type.
issues.evidence: Section 6 trigger list includes 'Listed building consent (if Grade I or II*, consult Historic England)'

issues.detail: Several Nutrient Neutrality tab_items are officer checks or form fragments, not applicant requirements: 'Is the Nitrate Vulnerable zone correct (check this at UK Soil Observatory)?', 'Has the default occupancy rate ... been used? (2.2 unless Esthwaite...)', 'Nutrient Neutrality Sign off 1st check Valid Invalid Who:', 'Exceptions to nutrient neutrality validation requirements;', and the garbled 'Householder development ... Are Nutrient Neutrality requirement met? yes no Does Natural England need consulting?' (householder is actually an exception). 'Any non-metric drawing ... should be returned. 4.' is an officer instruction.
issues.evidence: Natural England Annex 3 checklist and sign-off boxes at the end of the checklist

issues.detail: The Nutrient Neutrality items are filed under 'Policy-driven requirements (all application types)', but they apply only to sites within Natural England Nutrient Neutrality catchments, and only for new overnight accommodation, tourism development increasing day visitors, or agricultural development increasing stock. Householder, B2/B8, Class E and most F uses are excepted.
issues.evidence: Section 19: 'Within Natural England's Nutrient Neutrality Catchment Areas?' plus listed exceptions

issues.detail: 'Existing and proposed site levels / sections' and 'Floor plans / Elevations' share the same plans tick-box excerpt. 'Noise Impact Assessment' and 'Ventilation / Extraction details' are the same item (s16). 'Construction (Environmental) Management Plan' and 'Schedule of works (listed building)' share the same CMS excerpt.
issues.evidence: Section 3 Plans; section 16 Ventilation and Extraction

summary: Grokbot's link opens but has been superseded by the checklist reviewed on 6 August 2026 (BNG section rewritten). Its date of 2024-04-01 is also slightly wrong (the text says 2 April 2024). The extraction misses bat surveys, non-mains drainage, tree constraints plan, wind energy consultation and commercial impact assessment, invents rows such as 'Sunlight to gardens' and 'Schedule of works', and wrongly shows Householder and Listed building consent as having no local requirements.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
